ops.title: A Sprite desk host holds no token in its service environment
ops.body:
Since cc-skills #1850 (long-running 0.7.910, Nov 2 2026), a desk on a Sprite host gets its credentials three ways, and none sits in a Sprite service's environment, which `sprite-env services list` prints:

- AWS: short-lived STS session credentials, pushed from the Mac every 15 minutes into `desk-creds.py serve` memory, read through `credential_process`.
- Long-lived service tokens (Trunk, Buildkite read): AWS SSM Parameter Store, read at runner start through `host.ssm` with the STS profile `host.ssm_profile`. For durable-agents-rebuild: TRUNK_MERGE_API_KEY from /ci/tools/trunk-developer-api-key (the same value as the Mac Keychain item trunk-merge-api-key), BUILDKITE_TOKEN and BUILDKITE_API_TOKEN from /ci/tools/buildkite-read-token.
- The owner's GitHub token (writes must stay under his identity): a `host.secrets` entry, run on the Mac at each push and held in `serve` memory with a 45-minute expiry; `run` writes it only into the gh config under /dev/shm.

The Sprites org token never goes onto a Sprite (owner rule; root decision #327981). `serve` keeps the host awake through the Sprites Tasks API, not a `sprite exec` keepalive, and the landing adapter runs stack-enqueue in the host's own checkout instead of fanning out to dar-merge Sprites. If host load becomes the landing bottleneck, the path is an owner card about a Sprites custom_api connector wrapping api.sprites.dev (dashboard-only to create), never the token back on a Sprite.
